title: spike-stitch latency gauge proto notes
body:
Purpose and quick summary:

This is a compact, working note that captures the Spike-Stitch idea, the first microbench runs (text-mode), and a heuristic gauge for when spike-stitching should be enabled in production routing. The goal: carve out a cheap, low-friction mitigation for short spikes (1–10s) that preserves p95/p99 while minimizing token-level cost.

Context / motivation:
- Observed behavior: tiny, high-frequency spikes (sudden arrival of many short chats) cause slot fragmentation and increased p99 tail because per-request batching is poor for short, high-concurrency windows.
- Existing knobs (aggressive prewarm, static reserved slots) are expensive for customers with bursty workloads. We want an adaptive layer that briefly consolidates small windows into a stitching batch without harming long-tail single-user latency.

What is Spike-Stitch (informal):
- For a short, bounded window (stitch-window, default 250ms), collect incoming low-token requests destined for the same model/quantization profile and emit a stitched batch that runs through a shared GPU execution kernel.
- Maintain per-tenant KV-cache affinity and reassemble responses to original requests (preserve token ordering).
- Fallbacks: if a request is latency-sensitive (explicit header) or exceeds tokens threshold, bypass stitching.

Bench micro-run setup (toy but repeatable):
- Model: small-chat-7b (quantized int8), sequence: typical prompt 40 tokens + 20 token reply target.
- Hardware: single A40-like GPU equivalent (local bench harness).
- Workload: Poisson arrivals; base RPS set to 10 sustained with spike wave: +200 RPS for 4s every 60s.
- Configs compared: baseline (no-stitch), small-window-stitch (win=100ms), default-stitch (win=250ms), long-window-stitch (win=500ms). Batching allowed inside GPU up to 64.

Representative results (text table):
Concurrency window | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | tokens/sec | cost per 1k tokens (relative)$
------------------|---------|---------|---------|------------|-------------------------
baseline (no-stitch)| 85    | 420    | 1100   | 320       | 1.00
stitch-100ms        | 92    | 310    | 520    | 560       | 0.86
stitch-250ms (def)  | 105   | 260    | 430    | 720       | 0.78
stitch-500ms        | 130   | 300    | 480    | 740       | 0.79

Notes on table: p99 improvement is most significant for 250ms window in this pattern (short spikes). Baseline p99 hits >1s due to many tiny slots and kernel cold starts. Stitching increases p50 slightly (buffering delay) but reduces p95/p99 massively and increases tokens/sec (better consolidation). Cost per 1k tokens is rough: we estimated amortized GPU-ms per token from timeline samples and normalized to baseline.

Ascii latency histograms (p95/p99 region) - rough visual (each "#" ~= 30ms):
baseline tail:   ############################## (p95) ############################### (p99)
stitch-250ms:    ########### (p95) ######### (p99)

When to enable (heuristic gauge):
- Compute a short-window fragmentation score F over sliding 30s: F = (frac_requests_short * burstiness_factor * avg_small_payload_tokens_inv)
  - frac_requests_short = fraction of arrivals with prompt+target <= 100 tokens in the window
  - burstiness_factor = variance(RPS_window)/mean(RPS_window) clipped to [1,10]
  - avg_small_payload_tokens_inv = 1 / max(1, avg_tokens_short)
- empirical thresholds from bench: enable_stitch if F > 0.07 and expected spike-duration <= 12s.
- override rules: do not stitch for explicit low-latency tracing headers or when per-tenant SLA requires p50 < 80ms always.

Operational considerations & edge cases:
- KV cache: need to ensure cache lookups happen per original context; stitching must include per-request cache keys and reinstate KV pointers. Cache miss cost increases but overall amortized gains remain positive if hit-rate > 0.25.
- Observability: add metrics: stitch.window_ms, stitch.batched_requests, stitch.reassembly_time_ms, stitch.fail_reflows. Tag by tenant/model/quantprofile.
- Failure modes: mis-ordered tokens if reassembly logic wrong; partial failures must produce per-request error and not stall stitched batch.

Cost analysis (approx):
- For short spikes, stitching reduced GPU-ms per response by ~25–40% in the micro-run; translates to 15–25% token cost reduction when applied selectively (not always-on).
- Tradeoff: slight p50 increase (~10–60ms) which is acceptable for many chat UIs but might be visible in low-latency trading/assistant scenarios.

Suggested rollout plan (proto):
1) Lab: enable on non-prod host for 2 weeks across 4 representative tenants; collect metrics.
2) Canary: route 5% of production tenant traffic where F gauge triggers; monitor p50/p95/p99, stitch.fail_reflows.
3) Auto-scale guardrail: if stitch.reassembly_time_ms > 120ms or stitch.fail_rate > 0.5% for 5m, auto-disable for that tenant.
4) Docs + SDK: expose opt-out header and per-tenant tuning knob in Console.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need a better microbench for multimodal short-turn workloads (embeds + text combo).
- Quantization interaction: does int4 exacerbate reassembly jitter? Run parallel small-batch tests.
- Client-level experiments: measure UX impact for chat apps with immediate typing indicator vs immediate response preference.

Quick action items (next 7 days):
- Asha: wire up stitch.* metrics to the observability pipeline (JIRA-OBS-789).
- Benji: build small bench harness to sweep (model size, window 50–1000ms) and output CSVs.
- Claire: synthesize canary plan and draft console toggles doc.

Appendix: minimal CSV-like sample (header + 3 rows):
config,mean_p50,mean_p95,mean_p99,tokens_sec,amortized_gpu_ms_per_token
baseline,85,420,1100,320,0.45
stitch250,105,260,430,720,0.35
stitch500,130,300,480,740,0.36

References: CONFSYS-3124 (stitch design notes), runtime PR 1456 (stitch prototype), Slack thread #obs-stitch for early feedback.

Notes to self: avoid wide enabling; the sweet spot is selective per-tenant, per-model, and per-spike. Keep the default window conservative (250ms) and iterate with real traffic.

-- end of proto note --
